sections.bio:
I teach machines to think — and spend the rest of my day convincing humans that AI isn't as scary as it looks.

I'm an AI Developer at TaxTeck, where I build systems that sit at the intersection of AI and Data — from machine learning models and LLM-based applications to RAG pipelines and agentic AI workflows that actually do something useful, not just impressive in a demo.

What I work with:

 🔹 Machine Learning & LLMs — building models that solve real problems, not just notebook experiments
 🔹 RAG & Agentic AI — designing systems that retrieve, reason, and act, not just respond
 🔹 ETL & Data Pipelines — cleaning and structuring the messy data nobody wants to touch
 🔹 Analytics Automation — turning manual reporting into systems that run themselves

I didn't come from a "traditional" AI background — I learned most of this by breaking things first and understanding them later. That's exactly why I share what I learn: simple explanations of AI/Data concepts, honest lessons from real projects, and practical advice for anyone trying to break into this field without feeling lost in jargon.

No hype, no "AI will replace your job tomorrow" fear-mongering — just real work, explained like a human.
If you're into AI, Data, or just trying to figure out your path in tech, let's connect. I'm always up for a good conversation about models, pipelines, or why production AI never behaves like the tutorial said it would.

posts.text:
🚨 SCAM ALERT 🚨

I applied for an Operations Data Analyst position with high hopes.

After applying, I received an email saying I had been shortlisted for the technical assessment.

Everything looked completely normal. The email was professional, the process seemed genuine, and I was ready to prove my skills.

But when I clicked on the assessment link...

I was asked to pay ₹150 just to take the assessment.

Seriously?

Since when did job seekers have to pay to prove their skills?

Freshers are already spending money on education, certifications, internet, travel, and countless job applications. Now we're expected to pay just to participate in a hiring process?

This is not about ₹150.

It's about the message this sends:

 
"Pay first, then we'll decide whether you're good enough."

I strongly believe this is an unfair hiring practice. Candidates should be evaluated based on their talent, not their ability or willingness to pay an assessment fee.

I'm tagging Leap Finance Academy and Iskima and would genuinely appreciate a clarification on whether this is their official hiring policy.

If you believe job seekers deserve transparent and fair hiring, please Like, Comment, Repost, and share this post so more candidates become aware and companies take notice.

No candidate should have to pay to get a chance at a job.

DATA ANALYST v/s  DATA SCIENTIST

One of the most common questions I get is:

"What's the difference between a Data Analyst and a Data Scientist?" 🤔

While both work with data, their day-to-day work is quite different.

📊 Data Analyst
✅ Finds insights from data
✅ Creates dashboards & reports
✅ Helps businesses make better decisions
✅ Common tools: Excel, SQL, Power BI

🤖 Data Scientist
✅ Builds predictive models
✅ Works on Machine Learning & AI
✅ Solves complex data problems
✅ Common tools: Python, SQL, Statistics

💰 Both are high-demand careers.

But the real question isn't:

"Which one pays more?"
It's:

"Which one fits your interests and strengths better?"

If you enjoy dashboards, business insights, and storytelling with data → Data Analyst 📊

If you enjoy coding, statistics, machine learning, and predictions → Data Scientist 🤖

💬 If you had to choose one today, which would it be?

📊 Data Analyst
or
🤖 Data Scientist

👇 Let me know in the comments!

#DataAnalyst #DataScientist #DataAnalytics #DataScience #SQL #Python #MachineLearning #PowerBI #Analytics #CareerGrowth #BusinessIntelligence #DataJobs #CareerAdvice #LinkedInIndia #TechCareers

DATA ANALYST vs BUSINESS ANALYST

Two high-demand career paths.

Two different skill sets.

One common goal: solving problems and creating business impact.

🔹 Data Analysts work with data, dashboards, trends, and insights.

🔹 Business Analysts work with requirements, stakeholders, processes, and strategy.

💰 Average Salary (India)

📊 Data Analyst: ₹5–12 LPA

💼 Business Analyst: ₹6–15 LPA

The best role isn't the one with the higher salary.

It's the one that matches your strengths and interests.

So before choosing a career path, ask yourself:

👉 Do you enjoy working with data and numbers?

OR

👉 Do you enjoy solving business problems and communicating with people?

Which role would you choose?

Data Analyst or Business Analyst
